text:
Alex: Heads-up — Goldfinch v1 goes prod tomorrow 10:00 PDT. Early sims show a very different token profile (longer contexts, more rerank). We should finalize GPU-hour and routing plan today. :eyes:
Priya: ran a 6h spike sim against staging this morning. Aggregate tokens/sec up ~2.7x vs baseline for chat routes. Hot shards show KV cache churn -> per-request latency climbs at ~2.4M tokens/sec cluster-wide.
Marco: quick numbers from my run: baseline cluster steady-state ~115k t/s, Goldfinch sim ~310k t/s peak. If we want headroom for 1.5x unexpected surge, plan for ~465k t/s.
Jenna: region note — EU-west has limited spare A100 capacity next week (capacity calendar shows only ~24 GPUs free). Can't shift large volume to EU. US regions have room but will cost more if we burst to on-demand.
Li: networking flag — Goldfinch increases average response size; egress pressure on us-west-internal LB observed in staging (connection churn). Recommend bump connection limits and probe for NLB TCP flows.
Priya: translating to GPU-hours: to maintain latency SLOs at target load we need ~80 GPUs prewarmed during business-hours (M-F 08:00-20:00) and ~40 overnight. Rough weekly GPU-hours = (80*12*5) + (40*12*2) + (40*24*2) = 4800 + 960 + 1920 = 7680 GPU-hours/week. (That assumes 12h business windows.)
Marco: if we want full 24/7 hot reserve (simple approach) that's 80*24*7 = 13440 GPU-hours/week. Choose tradeoff: partial schedule vs full-time.
Sam: cost ballpark: committed GPU-hour rate we negotiate ~ $2.8/hr. Using Priya's partial schedule (7680 hrs/wk) -> ~ $21.5k/week -> ~$86k/month incremental. Full 24/7 (13440) -> ~$37.6k/week -> ~$150k/month.
Jenna: ops ask — can we autoscale instead to reduce committed spend? Autoscale works but cold-starts add latency. Suggest hybrid: reserved baseline (40 GPUs) + autoscale cap to 120 GPUs for bursts.
Priya: hybrid calc: baseline reserved 40 GPUs 24/7 = 6720 hrs/wk. Autoscale expected add ~2000 hrs/wk during launch -> total ~8720 hrs/wk. Cost ~ $24.4k/wk -> ~$106k/mo.
Marco: fallback policy: route low-priority calls to quantized variant goldfinch-q4 and keep high-priority traffic on full model. Expect q4 to reduce token GPU cost ~25%.
Sam: here's a suggested autoscale snippet to test in canary (config only):
```
autoscale_policy:
  min_instances: 10
  max_instances: 120
  scale_metric: tokens_per_sec
  target_value: 10000  # tokens/sec per instance (observed typical)
  cooldown: 120s
```
Alex: ops checklist for rollout: 1) prewarm 40 reserved GPUs in us-west and 16 in us-east by 09:30 PDT, 2) apply connection limit bumps Li suggested, 3) enable quantized fallback and routing rules, 4) set autoscale policy in canary, 5) monitoring alerts for KV-cache miss rate and p95 latency.
Li: I'll increase NLB connection limits and add extra connection-tracking nodes in us-west. Also will enable tcp_keepalive tuning on the proxy pool.
Jenna: I'll open a short-term reserved capacity request with cloud ops for +40 GPUs in us-west and +16 in us-east for the launch window. ETA approval ~2-3 hrs.
Priya: I'll run another 2h spike sim with the hybrid config (40 reserved + autoscale) and post the numbers in this thread.
ops-bot: Deploy scheduled for Goldfinch v1 at 2026-03-19T17:00:00Z by @deploy-bot :rocket:
Alex: Thanks all — if Priya's sim confirms hybrid looks OK we'll approve the reserved spend. If not, contingency is to cut some non-critical background eval traffic and reroute to lower-cost regions. :thumbsup:
Sam: one more thought — enable pack/prefill for multi-turns to reduce repeated prefix cost. Could shave 8-12% tokens/sec. I'll prototype tonight.
Priya: quick numbers will follow in ~2h. If anyone objects to the hybrid reserved + autoscale plan, speak now.
Alex: no objections so far, locking plan unless sim says otherwise.
